text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is using clear naming conventions. Variables and functions should have meaningful names, so readers know what they do without guessing. Another important point is keeping functions small and focused on one task. When functions do too many things, the code becomes confusing and hard to fix. Clean code is also easier to maintain. If you need to change something later, well-organized code saves time and reduces mistakes. In short, writing clean code helps everyone work faster and better.
